per_option_rationale.rationale: Computational slip giving 42 instead of 35, for example evaluating 7! / 4! = 210 and then dividing by 5 instead of 6.
Computed 7! / (5! x 2!) = 21 by shifting the factorial split by one step, treating the denominator as 5! x 2! instead of 4! x 3!.
Computed 7! / 4! = 210 and then divided only by 2 (using 2! = 2 from just the last factor 3, ignoring the full 3! = 6), giving 210 / 2 = 105.

explanation: Expand both factorial products: 7! = 5040, 4! = 24, 3! = 6, so denominator = 144, giving 5040 / 144 = 35.

explanation_sections.punchline: Factorials in numerator and denominator cancel step by step: 7x6x5 / (3x2x1) = 210 / 6 = 35.
explanation_sections.approach: Classify as a combination-style factorial ratio. Reduce by cancellation: 7! / (4! x 3!) = (7 x 6 x 5) / (3 x 2 x 1) = 35. Write out only the extra factors in the numerator above the larger factorial in the denominator.
explanation_sections.lesson: When evaluating n! / (k! x (n-k)!), cancel n! / k! first to get the n-k consecutive integers, then divide by (n-k)!.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 30 s by cancellation. Trap: computing full factorials and then dividing risks an arithmetic slip at the final step.
